Solution B is correct. Since 12 × 167 = 2004 exactly, the remainder is 0.

Solution A fails at its first step. It claims 12 divides evenly into 2000, but 2000 = 12 × 166 + 8, so 2000 leaves remainder 8. Its conclusion that 2004 leaves remainder 4 is therefore wrong.

Solution B's long division is also correct. 12 goes into 20 once (remainder 8), 12 goes into 80 six times (remainder 8), and 12 goes into 84 seven times (remainder 0). This gives quotient 167 and remainder 0.

WINNER: B
